title: Parliamentary vs presidential government
quote: Ambedkar: a democracy cannot maximise both stability and responsibility; India chose responsibility

boxes.title: Parliamentary features
items: Britain's system = ==**cooperation and co-ordination**== of legislature & executive (presidential = **separation of powers**)
**Nominal** head (President, de jure) vs **real** (PM + Council of Ministers); **Art. 74(1)** advice binding
**Majority party rule**: leader of majority in **Lok Sabha** = PM
**Dual membership**: non-member must be elected within ==**six months**==
PM = Head of Government, **Leader of the Lok Sabha**; lower House can be **dissolved**

cards.title: Semi-presidential
lines: Directly elected President + PM responsible to legislature

boxes.title: Merits & demerits
head: System
Merits
Demerits
rows: ==Responsible government==; harmony; fresh elections break deadlock
Unstable coalitions; no fixed tenure; cabinet dictatorship

boxes.title: Why the Constituent Assembly chose it & the debate
items: Familiar from ==**1919 and 1935 Acts**==; vast size & diversity
**One Nation, One Election**: Arts **83, 172, 327**; critics: presidential mechanics
**Shamsher Singh (1974)**: Governor criticising Cabinet runs counter to parliamentary system

boxes.title: Exam corner
items: A-R: parliamentary because executive responsible to legislature, R explains A (UPPSC 2025)
